title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a typed page, not a manuscript leaf: '- 149 - IX', section 12.1. It appears to be a page of the SGA 7 I typescript, Exposé IX (Grothendieck, 'Modèles de Néron et monodromie'), filed in the middle of the 1975-76 handwritten notes on cochain complexes C^*(X_•,F). The neighbouring pages are about simplicial and De Rham cochains and have no mathematical link to it.

Setting: S is the spectrum of a discrete valuation ring with generic point η. X → S is proper and flat with smooth generic fibre (a curve). X has factorial local rings, for instance X regular. P = Pic_{X/S} is the relative Picard functor, P^o its identity component, and E is the closure of the zero section of the generic fibre.

(b) E is described explicitly. Each irreducible component X_o^i of the special fibre is a Cartier divisor because the local rings are factorial (EGA IV 21.2.8.1). The invertible sheaf O_X(X_o^i) on X defines a section S_i of P over S, trivial at η. E is the subgroup generated by the S_i, and (12.1.6) says P^o ∩ E is the zero section.

(c) The quotient Q = P/E is representable by a smooth separated S-group scheme. It is 'néronien', meaning it satisfies the Néron mapping property (1.1.2).

(d) Assume moreover that the geometric generic fibre is integral. The degree map P → Z_S induces deg: Q → Z_S, giving an exact sequence 0 → A → Q → Z_S → 0 (12.1.8). Here A is smooth, separated and of finite type, and is the Néron model of the Jacobian A_η = P^o_η = Pic^o_{X_η/η} (12.1.9). Finally P^o → P → Q induces an isomorphism P^o ≅ A^o onto the identity component of the Néron model (12.1.10).

These are Raynaud's results on the Picard functor and Néron models of Jacobians (1970), recalled in SGA 7 IX §12 so they can be used for the monodromy and component-group analysis.
errors: The text has a notational inconsistency: O_X(X_o^i) in one place and O_X(X_i^o) in the next line. It is the same divisor; the typescript itself carries the slip.
'le faisceau inversible O_X(X_o^i) sur S' is loose wording: the sheaf lives on X and defines a section of P over S.

Raynaud's theorems need hypotheses beyond those stated on this page, such as regularity of X, and a gcd-of-multiplicities or cohomological-flatness condition for the identity-component statements. These are presumably contained in the 'conditions de b)' set out on the previous page of the typescript, which is not shown here.

ideas.what: E, the closure of the unit section in Pic_{X/S}, is generated by the classes of O_X(component of the special fibre); P^o ∩ E is trivial
ideas.modern_name: Closure of the unit section in the Picard functor of a regular model
ideas.usually_credited_to: M. Raynaud, 'Spécialisation du foncteur de Picard' (Publ. IHÉS 38, 1970)

ideas.what: Pic_{X/S}/E is a smooth separated group scheme satisfying the Néron property
ideas.modern_name: Raynaud's theorem: Néron model of a Jacobian via the Picard functor of a regular proper model
ideas.usually_credited_to: M. Raynaud 1970; textbook account in Bosch–Lütkebohmert–Raynaud, Néron Models, ch. 9

ideas.what: Exact sequence 0 → A → Q → Z → 0 with A the Néron model of Pic^o, and P^o ≅ A^o
ideas.modern_name: Néron model of the Jacobian as the degree-zero part of Pic/E; identity component equals Pic^0_{X/S}

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typescript page of SGA 7 I Exposé IX, published in 1972. It recalls Raynaud's well-known results on Picard functors and Néron models, which are standard and correctly credited. It sits in this folder only as a filed document and has no bearing on the surrounding De Rham and simplicial-cochain notes.
transcription_corrections: The page is a typed SGA 7 IX typescript page, not handwritten notes; '467' is the archive pagination and '62' the folder page number.
'O_X(X_i^o)' faithfully reproduces the typescript's own inconsistent notation; it should read O_X(X_o^i).
In the third paragraph of d) 'un sc[h]éma' has a handwritten mark over the 'h'; the reading 'schéma' is correct.
